basis: Earth-reference planetary parameters inherited from V0.6; circulation is a conceptual first-order model, not a numerical climate simulation.

circulation_cells_each_hemisphere.hadley: approximately 0°–30°; rising motion concentrated near the migrating ITCZ and subsidence in the subtropics
circulation_cells_each_hemisphere.ferrel: approximately 30°–60°; mid-latitude eddy-driven circulation, not a simple thermally direct cell
circulation_cells_each_hemisphere.polar: approximately 60°–90°; cold polar air and polar-front interaction

pressure_belts.name: Equatorial low / ITCZ
pressure_belts.approximate_latitude: near 0°, with seasonal migration generally several degrees into the summer hemisphere

pressure_belts.name: Polar highs
pressure_belts.approximate_latitude: toward high polar latitudes; not drawn as a fixed boundary

prevailing_surface_winds.name: Northeast trade winds
prevailing_surface_winds.direction: east to west, with equatorward component

prevailing_surface_winds.name: Southeast trade winds
prevailing_surface_winds.direction: east to west, with equatorward component

atmospheric_model.seasonal_behavior: Pressure belts and the ITCZ migrate with the seasonal shift of maximum solar heating. Continents, mountains, sea-surface temperatures and transient weather systems distort the idealized zonal pattern.

ocean_circulation.status: Not geographically plotted; basin topology and bathymetry are insufficiently validated.
broad_expectations: Subtropical gyres may form in sufficiently large, connected ocean basins under trade winds and westerlies.
Equatorial surface currents are commonly westward, while equatorial countercurrents can flow eastward in some basins.
Western boundary currents are commonly narrow and poleward; eastern boundary currents are commonly broader and equatorward.
These are general Earth-like tendencies, not a commitment that every basin on this planet has a complete gyre or a named current.
withheld_decisions: Number, centers, boundaries and exact paths of ocean gyres
Current speed, temperature anomaly and seasonal strength
Upwelling zones and deep-ocean overturning circulation

map_representation.method: Schematic latitude bands and directional arrows placed on the existing linear latitude-longitude drawing.
map_representation.note: The overlay is an explanatory diagram. It does not trace actual winds around terrain or coastlines and is not a projection-correct global circulation map.

limitations: Atmospheric composition, surface pressure, atmospheric mass, greenhouse forcing, cloud feedback and humidity remain unspecified.
Topography, mountain chains, elevation, bathymetry and detailed coastline-to-ocean-basin geometry remain incomplete.
The circulation cells and wind belts are approximate Earth-like climatological averages; actual winds vary by season and weather.
The map uses a provisional linear SVG scaffold rather than a validated cartographic projection.
No specific ocean current, biome, desert, rainfall regime or regional climate is assigned.
All content remains NON-CANON until explicitly approved.
